subproblem.title: Boundary rectifiability for compactly supported currents in ℝ^P from the deformation theorem and CL(d)
subproblem.statement: Assume (DT), the exact frozen statement of cmc_deformation_theorem (first hypothesis of the Lean statement). For every P, m there is c ≥ 1 such that for all ρ > 0, compact K and Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, every integer multiplicity T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with spt T ⊆ K, M(T) ≤ Λ and M(∂T) < ∞ decomposes as T − Q − S = ∂R. Here Q, ∂Q, R are integer multiplicity, M(∂Q) ≤ cM(∂T), M(R) ≤ cρM(T) and M(S) ≤ cρM(∂T) (plus further conclusions not used here). Let d ∈ ℕ and assume CL(d), verbatim: for all P, open U ⊆ ℝ^P and integer multiplicity T_j ∈ 𝒟_d(U) with sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U, and T_j ⇀ T ∈ 𝒟_d(U), T is integer multiplicity. Let P ∈ ℕ, T ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) integer multiplicity, and K ⊆ ℝ^P compact with spt T ⊆ K, M(T) < ∞ and M(∂T) < ∞. Then ∂T is integer multiplicity.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P m : ℕ), ∃ c : NNReal, 1 ≤ c ∧ ∀ (ρ : ℝ) (K : Set (Euclid P)) (Λ : NNReal), 0 < ρ → IsCompact K → ∃ 𝒬 : Set (GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), 𝒬.Finite ∧ ∀ T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity T → T.support ⊆ K → T.mass ≤ Λ → T.boundary.mass < ∞ → ∃ Q ∈ 𝒬, ∃ (R : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 2)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), IsIntegerMultiplicity Q ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity Q.boundary ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity R ∧ T - Q - S = R.boundary ∧ (Q = 0 ∨ ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ (m + 1)) ≤ Q.mass) ∧ Q.mass ≤ c * T.mass ∧ Q.boundary.mass ≤ c * T.boundary.mass ∧ R.mass ≤ c * ENNReal.ofReal ρ * T.mass ∧ S.mass ≤ c * ENNReal.ofReal ρ * T.boundary.mass ∧ Q.support ∪ R.support ⊆ thickening (3 * Real.sqrt P * ρ) T.support ∧ Q.boundary.support ∪ S.support ⊆ thickening (3 * Real.sqrt P * ρ) T.boundary.support) → ∀ d : ℕ, (∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U d) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U d), IsOpen U → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j)) → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → ⨆ j, ((Ts j).massOn W + boundaryMassOn (Ts j) W) < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn Ts T → IsIntegerMultiplicity T) → ∀ (P : ℕ) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1)) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → T.support ⊆ K → T.mass < ∞ → T.boundary.mass < ∞ → IsIntegerMultiplicity T.boundary
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Steps 7–9 (Simon Ch. 6, 6.2, first case U = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with M(T), M(∂T) < ∞: the scaled deformation theorem with ρ = ρ_k ↓ 0 gives P_k ⇀ T with M(∂P_k) ≤ cM(∂T); and 6.3: combine this with the closure theorem). Uses the siblings cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn (key eval_bound) and rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props (key norm_props; part (iv), continuity of |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm). Both are comparator-accepted declarations reused at their frozen types. All masses are taken in the domain ℝ^P, so M(X) = M_{ℝ^P}(X) = X.massOn univ.
1. Constants. (DT) with (P, m := d) gives c ∈ ℝ≥0 with c ≥ 1. Let Λ := M(T) ∈ ℝ≥0; this is possible because M(T) is finite, and then M(T) ≤ Λ (ENNReal.coe_toNNReal).
2. Approximants. For k ∈ ℕ put ρ_k := 2^{−k} > 0. Apply (DT) with ρ_k, K and Λ to T; T is integer multiplicity, spt T ⊆ K, M(T) ≤ Λ and M(∂T) < ∞. This gives Q_k, S_k ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) and R_k ∈ 𝒟_{d+2}(ℝ^P) such that ∂Q_k is integer multiplicity, T − Q_k − S_k = ∂R_k, M(∂Q_k) ≤ cM(∂T), M(R_k) ≤ cρ_kM(T) and M(S_k) ≤ cρ_kM(∂T). Choose such currents for every k.
3. Sup bounds for test forms. Let m ∈ ℕ and ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P). The function x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous, because |·| is continuous by rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props (iv) and ω is smooth. It has compact support, because ω does and |0| = 0 (HasCompactSupport.comp_left). So it is bounded (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous). Taking the maximum of a bound with 1 gives C_ω > 0 with |ω(x)| ≤ C_ω for every x.
4. Weak convergence Q_k ⇀ T. Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(ℝ^P) and put C₁ := C_ω and C₂ := C_{dω}, where dω ∈ 𝒟^{d+2}(ℝ^P).
 - Subtraction of currents is pointwise, so evaluating T − Q_k − S_k = ∂R_k at ω gives T(ω) − Q_k(ω) − S_k(ω) = ∂R_k(ω) = R_k(dω). Hence |Q_k(ω) − T(ω)| ≤ |S_k(ω)| + |R_k(dω)|.
 - M(S_k) ≤ cρ_kM(∂T) < ∞ and M(R_k) ≤ cρ_kM(T) < ∞. So cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn with W := ℝ^P gives |S_k(ω)| ≤ C₁·M(S_k) and |R_k(dω)| ≤ C₂·M(R_k), with the finite masses read as real numbers. In [0, ∞] this reads ofReal|S_k(ω)| ≤ ofReal(C₁)·M(S_k) ≤ ofReal(C₁)·cρ_kM(∂T) and ofReal|R_k(dω)| ≤ ofReal(C₂)·M(R_k) ≤ ofReal(C₂)·cρ_kM(T) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
 - So ofReal|Q_k(ω) − T(ω)| ≤ ofReal(ρ_k)·A with A := C₁cM(∂T) + C₂cM(T) < ∞. Taking toReal (ENNReal.toReal_mono) gives |Q_k(ω) − T(ω)| ≤ ρ_k·A.toReal.
 - The right side tends to 0 as k → ∞ (tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one, squeeze_zero). Hence Q_k(ω) → T(ω) for every ω, i.e. Q_k ⇀ T in ℝ^P.
5. Boundaries. ∂Q_k ⇀ ∂T in ℝ^P (WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary; Simon 2.3 and 2.13).
6. Uniform local bounds. Let W be open.
 - M_W(∂Q_k) ≤ M_{ℝ^P}(∂Q_k) = M(∂Q_k) ≤ cM(∂T) (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono).
 - boundaryMassOn(∂Q_k, W) = 0. If d = 0, this holds by definition: the boundary mass of a 0-current is 0. If d = m + 1, it equals M_W(∂∂Q_k) = M_W(0) by GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary, and M_W(0) = 0 because every admissible value is ofReal(0) = 0.
 Hence sup_k (M_W(∂Q_k) + boundaryMassOn(∂Q_k, W)) ≤ cM(∂T) < ∞, since c < ∞ and M(∂T) < ∞ (ENNReal.mul_lt_top).
7. Closure. Apply CL(d) with P, U := ℝ^P (open), T_k := ∂Q_k (integer multiplicity by step 2), the bound of step 6 and the convergence of step 5. Hence ∂T is integer multiplicity. ∎

subproblem.title: A compactly supported current in ℝ^P has mass and boundary mass at most those of its restriction to an open set containing its support
subproblem.statement: Assume (VO): for all P, n, U ⊆ ℝ^P, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0 (the exact frozen statement dtc_vanish_off_support, appearing verbatim as the first hypothesis). Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, C ⊆ U compact and Y ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) with spt Y ⊆ C. Then M(Y) ≤ M(Y|_U) and M(∂Y) ≤ M(∂(Y|_U)), where Y|_U = Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U).

1. Y vanishes off C. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ∩ C = ∅. Since spt Y ⊆ C, tsupport ω ∩ spt Y = ∅, so Y(ω) = 0 by (VO).
2. ∂Y vanishes off C. Let η ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) with tsupport η ∩ C = ∅. Then ∂Y(η) = Y(dη) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply). Also tsupport dη ⊆ tsupport η (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), so ∂Y(η) = 0 by step 1.
3. Localizing the masses. C is compact, U is open and C ⊆ U. Apply lcmp_massOn_le_of_vanish_off_compact with V := U and the arbitrary set ℝ^P, to Y (by step 1) and to ∂Y (by step 2). This gives M(Y) = M_{ℝ^P}(Y) ≤ M_U(Y) and M(∂Y) = M_{ℝ^P}(∂Y) ≤ M_U(∂Y).
4. Comparison with a restriction. Let m ∈ ℕ, Z ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) and Z' ∈ 𝒟_m(U) with Z(ιω) = Z'(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(U). We show M_U(Z) ≤ M_U(Z') = M(Z'). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) be admissible for M_U(Z), i.e. tsupport ω ⊆ U and |ω| ≤ 1. The same form is a test form with tsupport ⊆ U, so it defines ω' ∈ 𝒟^m(U) with ιω' = ω, and ω' is admissible for M_U(Z'). 6. Combining steps 3–5: M(Y) ≤ M_U(Y) ≤ M(Y|_U) and M(∂Y) ≤ M_U(∂Y) ≤ M(∂(Y|_U)). ∎
